retention_at_final.why: below this the student sits so far from the teacher surface that a contrast between two arms is dominated by early-imitability rather than by the factor under test (Codex pass 2, MAJOR-9)

late_slope.why: a curve still climbing steeply at the final checkpoint is an early-training snapshot, and its ranking need not survive to final dose

kind: a BUDGET TRIGGER, not a calibrated ranking-adequacy test. Neither threshold is tied to a measured rank-concordance rate, and the slope is a two-point difference read where the cosine schedule has already decayed the LR to 1e-5 -- so a small late gain can mean the schedule shut learning down rather than that the representation converged (Codex pass 3). It is used only to decide whether spending stage B is worth it; it certifies nothing
